newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks inch higher, Repsol shines.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks inch higher, Repsol shines.

text.p: Madrid stocks climbed to close higher on Tuesday and traders said they were optimistic about the medium-term outlook for the market, although they would not rule out volatility in the short term.
The general index rose 1.87 points, 0.39 percent, to 478.22, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares climbed 21.66 points, 0.4 percent, to 5,482.79.
"The market is firm and unless Wall Street dictates otherwise, we'll continue with this recovery," one trader said.
Repsol, undergoing the privatisation of the government's last 10.0 percent stake, broke the key 6,000 pesetas level and outperformed the market, rising 50 pesetas, or 0.84 percent, to 6,010.
Traders said the market would remain focused on Spain's March CPI data due on Friday, seen up around 2.4 percent year- on-year or lower, versus 2.5 percent in February.
Turnover remained high with Telefonica and Iberdrola accounting for 46.8 percent of volume.
Telefonica ended 10 pesetas higher at 3,400, while Iberdrola rose 30 pesetas to 1,625.
